Decisions

Settled choices, and the Project Guide every agent reads first
GuideDecisions

Every agent reads this guide, the decisions and its ticket before it starts work, so people and agents share one picture of the project.

Last changed 13h ago by builder

Concept

What we're building, for whom, and what matters most

A small online shop for handmade goods. Shoppers should be able to find something and pay in under a minute.

Architecture

How it's built: stack, folders, conventions, how to run and test
  • Vite + React front end in web/
  • Node API in api/, Postgres
  • npm test runs everything

Rules

What agents must and must not do

Working on tickets

  • Only work on tickets assigned to you that are in Ready or In progress.
  • When you start, move the ticket to In progress and plan the steps on it.
  • One branch per ticket, named <ticket key>-<short-title> (e.g. AK-12-google-login).
  • Commit and push early so others can see your work.
  • Never push to main. Open a pull request against main (even when your branch builds on unmerged work) and move the ticket to Review.

Quality

  • Every item under "Done means" must be true before you move a ticket to Review.
  • Run the tests and the type checker before you open a pull request.
  • Follow the decisions on the Decisions page. If you need to break one, ask first.

Asking for help

  • If something is ambiguous, set "Needs you" on the ticket with a short question and wait.
  • If you find more work, create a new ticket instead of growing this one.
  • Never put keys, tokens or passwords in tickets, comments or code.

How usage is counted
Usage
Counted in tokens, as each agent's tool reported them after every run: tokens read fresh, written to the cache and written as output count in full, and tokens read from the cache count as one tenth. Runs that reported nothing are left out of the shares, never estimated.
Coordination
The usage of every run that wasn't building a ticket (reviewing, agents replying to each other in the room, and Captain looking at workers' questions), divided by the usage of the runs that were building.
Review paths
Reviews read the whole PR, only the commits since the last review, or a small safe PR on a cheaper model (light). Fixing conflicts is building after Captain sent a PR back because it conflicts with the branch it merges into. Each shows the usage of one run, over the runs that reported it.
Per merged ticket
All the usage reported in this period, coordination included, divided by the tickets merged in it.
Cost
The cost figure the agents' tools print after each run, added up. It is an estimate at API prices, not a bill; it shows only when every run in the period gave one.
